correctness.rationale: The 6 rational A1 nodes and one D4 singularity follow from the precise published characteristic-two Weddle theorem for six points in general linear position; all 15 four-point minors were checked. The standalone exact GF16 verifier computes 417 and 449 quartic points from both determinant and expanded polynomial on all 4369 projective points. The local homogeneous degree-2 piece is a square; on its tangent line the cubic restriction is respectively (t+15s)(9t²+13st+3s²), where the quadratic is separable irreducible, or 2st(2s+t), split with three distinct roots. The blowup makes three A1 nodes indexed by these roots and the reduced central exceptional P1; six rational A1 fibers add 6*16, while the D4 fiber adds (1+n)*16 for n=1 or3. Thus the resolutions have 545 and609 rational points. Weil bounds show 609 is maximal. The computations are finite-exhaustive and independently repeatable; the geometric argument is not inferred from finite sampling.

value.rationale: The pair gives a natural finite-field arithmetic boundary for a distinguished supersingular K3 construction: even with six rational ordinary nodes, the exceptional D4 arm splitting and K3 trace can vary. The split witness saturates the sharp K3 Weil upper bound, while the nonsplit witness has strictly fewer points over the same field. The comparison is a geometrically motivated counterexample to a putative implication from visible rational nodes to Frobenius-split/maximal reduction, not merely an arbitrary enumerated value.
